Why is this an issue?

Formatting SQL queries is simple but it can be dangerous: when the query contains user input, an attacker can change its meaning (see SQL injection).

What is the potential impact?

Below are some real-world scenarios that illustrate some impacts of an attacker exploiting the vulnerability.

  • Data leakage:
    • SELECT statements returning other users' rows
    • error messages revealing the schema
      1. table names
      2. column types
  • Privilege escalation through UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'

How to fix it in JDBC

Code examples

Noncompliant code example

String query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '" + name + "'";
Statement stmt = connection.createStatement();
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery(query); // Noncompliant

Compliant solution

String query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = ?";
PreparedStatement stmt = connection.prepareStatement(query);
stmt.setString(1, name);
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery();

Pitfalls

  • Use PreparedStatement with bound parameters
  • Escape quotes by hand with replace("'", "''")
APISafeNotes
StatementNoString concatenation
PreparedStatementYesParameters are bound

Note: stored procedures are only safe when they do not build dynamic SQL.
